summary: Nine comment-endorsed discoveries spanning developer tools, electronics, books and visual mathematics.
telegram_footer: 9 items surfaced | 30/30 past front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated

items.name: django-paradedb
items.source_story_title: Do we still have to denormalize? Have your schema and search it too
items.summary: Django integration bringing ranked, fuzzy and hybrid search to PostgreSQL QuerySets.
items.why_included: Direct praise for keeping search inside the existing database and ORM.
items.evidence: A commenter praises ParadeDB's Django integration for BM25 scoring, fuzzy matching, hybrid search and avoiding a separate search engine.

evidence_sources.author: anon373839
evidence_sources.excerpt: ParadeDB is the best! I really like the Django integration (https://github.com/paradedb/django-paradedb). You get proper BM25 scoring, fuzzy matching, hybrid search, metadata filtering while still just using QuerySets.

items.name: Chrono
items.source_story_title: Jiff 1.0: A datetime library for Rust
items.summary: Rust date-and-time library praised for dependable standard-library and embedded use.
items.why_included: Strong first-hand endorsement of a concrete alternative in the Jiff discussion.
items.evidence: A user calls Chrono the best datetime library they have used; its original author acknowledges shortcomings in the API.

evidence_sources.author: the__alchemist
evidence_sources.excerpt: Chrono is by far, the best datetime library I've used.

evidence_sources.author: lifthrasiir
evidence_sources.excerpt: that's why the API is not very good, despite my best efforts

items.name: mini.nvim
items.summary: Independent Neovim Lua modules you can pick individually rather than installing wholesale.
items.why_included: An existing user explicitly endorses the modular pick-and-choose approach.
items.evidence: A user reports using four mini plugins in a ten-plugin setup and being happy with their functionality.

evidence_sources.author: eikenberry
evidence_sources.excerpt: I currently use 4 mini.* plugins out of the 10 plugins I use and am happy with what they do.

items.name: reTerminal E1004
items.summary: Framed 13.3-inch color e-paper display endorsed as a battery-powered family calendar.
items.why_included: A practical family-dashboard recommendation with first-hand battery-life evidence.
items.evidence: An owner uses the E1004 for a family calendar, praises the displays and reports one to two months of battery life.

evidence_sources.author: kimos
evidence_sources.excerpt: I’ve been using a couple of the ReTerminal displays and they’re great. I use the e1004 13” for a family calendar/schedule board. It comes framed and the battery lasts a month or two.

items.name: OOS
items.source_story_title: OOS – an open operating system for the Rigol Scopes
items.summary: Open operating system for Rigol oscilloscopes, praised for its ambitious hardware integration.
items.why_included: Independent praise goes beyond curiosity to a specific hardware-buying recommendation.
items.evidence: A commenter describes OOS as impressive and says its availability makes a Rigol worth choosing over competing brands.

evidence_sources.author: pseudohadamard
evidence_sources.excerpt: it's actually worth getting a Rigol over other similar brands just for this.

items.name: VSBHDA
items.source_story_title: Winudf – DVD / BluRay driver for DOS, Windows 1.x – 3x / 95 / 98 / ME
items.summary: Sound Blaster emulation for DOS, recommended for retro-computing sound-driver needs.
items.why_included: A specific preferred driver surfaced inside an unrelated optical-disc driver thread.
items.evidence: A commenter explicitly prefers VSBHDA for sound and encourages contributing relevant fixes there.

evidence_sources.author: vkaku
evidence_sources.excerpt: I'd prefer using VSBHDA driver for Sound though. If you have any fixes for those cards see if you can land them there.

items.name: The Secret Life of Circuits
items.summary: Michal Zalewski’s illustrated electronics book, enthusiastically recommended for engaging circuit-design teaching.
items.why_included: An unambiguous reading recommendation with a verified publisher link.
items.evidence: A commenter calls the book an exceptionally engaging electronics read and urges readers to thank its author.

evidence_sources.author: laxisOp
evidence_sources.excerpt: I cant recommend any better and engaging electronics book than this .

items.name: A Seventh Man
items.source_story_title: The Lasting Influence of John Berger
items.summary: John Berger and Jean Mohr’s illustrated exploration of migrant workers’ lives in Europe.
items.why_included: A concrete book singled out as Berger's best work, not merely a mention of the author.
items.evidence: A commenter ranks A Seventh Man as Berger's best work and quotes its argument about understanding others' constrained choices.

evidence_sources.author: zero_k
evidence_sources.excerpt: John Berger is amazing, and his "Seventh Man" (title based on an amazing Hungarian poem) is IMO his best work

items.name: The Continuity of Splines
items.summary: Freya Holmér’s visual explanation of splines and the mathematics behind smooth curves.
items.why_included: A directly recommended learning resource from a discussion of geometric smoothness.
items.evidence: A commenter calls the linked spline-continuity video amazing.
